purpose: Create an instance of a container from an OCI bundle (config.json + rootfs). All config.json properties EXCEPT process.args are applied; user process is not started until `runc start`. Container appears in `runc list` with state `created`.

flags.name: --console-socket
flags.doc: AF_UNIX socket to receive the pty master fd via SCM_RIGHTS. Required if config.json's process.terminal=true.

flags.name: --pid-file
flags.doc: Write the initial container process pid to this file.

flags.name: --no-pivot
flags.doc: Don't use pivot_root; chroot+chdir instead. Discouraged: 'may be unsafe from a security standpoint'.

flags.name: --no-new-keyring
flags.doc: Don't create a new session keyring; container inherits the caller's.

flags.name: --preserve-fds
flags.doc: Pass N additional fds beyond stdio + $LISTEN_FDS.

examples.expected_output: creates resources; `runc state c1` returns status=created

examples.expected_output: creates and writes pid to file; pty master delivered to console-socket

purpose: Shortcut for `create` + `start` — creates and starts a container in one go. Most common for one-off / interactive use. Default attached; `--detach` for backgrounded.

flags.name: --console-socket
flags.doc: AF_UNIX socket for pty master fd.

flags.name: --no-subreaper
flags.doc: Don't use PR_SET_CHILD_SUBREAPER. Reaping then falls to whoever wraps runc.

flags.name: --keep
flags.doc: Keep state directory and cgroup after exit (manual `runc delete` required after). Useful for inspecting cgroup state of an exited container.

examples.expected_output: runs config.json's process.args attached to caller's stdio

purpose: Execute a new process inside a running container. Two forms: command-line + flags, or full process spec from a JSON file. Exits with the command's exit status (255 on internal error).

flags.name: --cwd
flags.doc: Working dir inside container before exec.

flags.name: --process, -p
flags.doc: Use a process spec JSON file (full OCI process spec) instead of CLI flags.

flags.name: --cap
flags.doc: Add capability to the bounding set. Repeatable.

flags.name: --ignore-paused
flags.doc: Allow exec in a paused container (default errors out).

flags.name: --cgroup
flags.doc: Run in a sub-cgroup. v1: per-controller mappings; v2: single path.

purpose: Send signal to container's pid 1. Default SIGTERM. No grace period at this layer — that's containerd / dockerd. Errors if state is not `created` or `running`.

flags.name: <signal>
flags.doc: Signal name (with or without SIG prefix) or numeric value. Default SIGTERM.

purpose: Delete resources held by a container. Container must be in `stopped` state unless `--force`. Deletes only what runc created — pre-existing resources are left alone.

flags.name: --force, -f
flags.doc: SIGKILL the running container first, then delete.

purpose: Output current state of a container as JSON: ociVersion, id, status (creating|created|running|stopped), pid, bundle, annotations.

purpose: Generate a starter `config.json` in the bundle dir. ALWAYS needs editing afterwards (default sets process.args=["sh"], which fails on most images). Pair with `jq` to mutate.

flags.name: --bundle, -b
flags.doc: Bundle dir to drop config.json into (default: cwd).

flags.name: --rootless
flags.doc: Generate a rootless-friendly spec (no setgroups, user namespace, mapped uids). Distinct from runc's global --rootless.

purpose: containerd's bundled debug CLI. Native API (NOT CRI). Subcommands grouped by service: images (pull/push/ls/rm/import/export), containers (create/ls/info/rm), tasks (start/ls/kill/exec/pause/resume), namespaces, content, snapshots, events, version, plugins. 'For debugging only' per the official docs — use nerdctl for general purpose.
